SUMMARY: Ledgerline error blocking PO save when a lithium-cell item lacks a valid UN 38.3 certificate under setting PUR.CERT_CHK='B'.
INFOBOX:
code: ERR-SUP-0208
message: UN38.3 CERTIFICATE MISSING OR EXPIRED
module: PUR
screen: PUR-PO-01
introduced: RN-7.2.3-P6 (2026-10-26)
status: current
CONFLICTS:
- none
BODY:
`ERR-SUP-0208 UN38.3 CERTIFICATE MISSING OR EXPIRED` is a Ledgerline error introduced in [[rn-7-2-3-p6|RN-7.2.3-P6]] on 26 October 2026 [^r1]. It blocks saving a purchase order when the configuration requires an active [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] for lithium-cell items [^r1].

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Error code | ERR-SUP-0208 |
| Message | UN38.3 CERTIFICATE MISSING OR EXPIRED |
| Module | PUR |
| Screen | [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01]] |
| Introduced | [[rn-7-2-3-p6|RN-7.2.3-P6]] (2026-10-26) |
| Status | Current |

## Meaning
The system refuses the save operation because an order line includes a lithium-cell item from a supplier without a qualifying certificate valid on the order date [^r1].

## Cause
The error triggers when configuration parameter `PUR.CERT_CHK` is set to `'B'` and an order line contains a lithium-cell item whose supplier has no UN 38.3 certificate valid on the purchase order date [^r1].

## How to fix
Provide a valid UN 38.3 certificate for the supplier covering the order date, or adjust the line or configuration requirements before saving [^r1].

## Raised by
Raised on Save within screen [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01]] via the purchase order save validation logic [^r1].

## See also
* [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01 Purchase Order Entry]]

title: Tax codes
type: topic

Tax codes determine VAT handling on purchase orders and supplier invoices across Ledgerline ERP modules. Effective 26 October 2026 under [[rn-7-2-3-p6|RN-7.2.3-P6]], the Fetch routine automatically assigns designated tax codes based on supplier jurisdiction to ensure compliance with domestic and cross-border VAT requirements[^r1]. Incorrect tax code assignments trigger validation errors during purchase order processing on [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01 Purchase Order Entry]].

## Tax code assignment

Under Ledgerline 7.2.3-P6, Fetch assigns tax code `VAT20-UK` for GB suppliers[^r1]. For non-GB overseas suppliers, Fetch automatically assigns tax code `VAT20-RC`[^r1]. This logic is executed by the purchase order fetch services in [[services-pur-po|PUR po services]] when loading supplier records into purchase transactions[^r1].

Mismatches between the assigned tax code and supplier geographic region prevent document release and trigger [[err-po-0412|ERR-PO-0412 TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY]].

---
title: RN-7.2.3-P6 Ledgerline ERP 7.2.3-P6 Patch Notes
type: release
slug: rn-7-2-3-p6
summary: Patch notes for Ledgerline ERP 7.2.3-P6, covering automated tax code selection on PO fetch and parameterised UN 38.3 certificate blocking.
audience: staff
sources:
  - RN-7.2.3-P6
status: current
created: 2026-10-26
updated: 2026-10-26
---

Ledgerline ERP patch 7.2.3-P6 was released on 23 October 2026 and installed at Northbridge Cycles on 26 October 2026 at 07:00 under change CR-2026-034[^r1]. The patch introduces automated tax code assignment by supplier country on purchase order fetch and adds an optional hard block for missing or expired lithium-cell UN 38.3 certificates[^r2][^r4]. As of 26 October 2026, the automated tax code resolution is active, while automated certificate blocking remains disabled pending review in January 2027[^r7][^r8].

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| Version | 7.2.3-P6 |
| Release date | 2026-10-23 |
| Installation date | 2026-10-26 |
| Change request | CR-2026-034 |
| Status | current |
| Module | PUR |

## Changes

In 7.2.3-P6, Fetch (F3, service po_fetch on [[services-pur-po|PUR po services]]) fills the tax code from the supplier's country: VAT20-UK for GB suppliers and VAT20-RC for suppliers in any other country[^r2]. Prior to this patch, Fetch always populated VAT20-UK, which triggered [[err-po-0412|ERR-PO-0412]] for overseas suppliers[^r3].

Parameter PUR.CERT_CHK accepts a third value, 'B' (block), which refuses Save on [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01]] for items with the lithium-cell flag with [[err-sup-0208|ERR-SUP-0208]] if no valid certificate exists on the order date[^r4]. Under PUR.CERT_CHK, setting value 'Y' continues to issue only warning W-SUP-0207, while the parameter default remains 'N'[^r5]. The certificate check in 7.2.3-P6 evaluates only the valid-to date and does not enforce company rules regarding issue dates or margins[^r6].

## Effect at Northbridge

The automated Fetch tax code behaviour is live at Northbridge Cycles from 26 October 2026, so buyers no longer need to manually change VAT20-UK to VAT20-RC for overseas suppliers[^r8].

At Northbridge Cycles, parameter PUR.CERT_CHK remains set to 'N' following CAB CR-2026-031 to review in January 2027, keeping the manual check in [[sop-pur-001|SOP-PUR-001]] as the active control[^r7].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Tax code determination on Fetch**: Today's rule under 7.2.3-P6 is that Fetch sets VAT20-UK for GB vendors and VAT20-RC for non-GB vendors[^r2]. Previously, Fetch defaulted to VAT20-UK for all suppliers, requiring manual correction to avoid [[err-po-0412|ERR-PO-0412]] (superseded)[^r3].
* **UN 38.3 certificate enforcement**: The system supports automated blocking on Save via parameter PUR.CERT_CHK value 'B' and error [[err-sup-0208|ERR-SUP-0208]][^r4]. However, Northbridge maintains PUR.CERT_CHK as 'N' under CAB CR-2026-031 until January 2027, relying strictly on the manual verification procedure in [[sop-pur-001|SOP-PUR-001]] (rule_not_in_policy)[^r7].

| | |
|---|---|
| code | ERR-PO-0412 |

`ERR-PO-0412` is a validation error raised by the Ledgerline purchase order module when an order line tax code does not match the supplier account's recorded country [^r1][^r4][^r18]. It occurs on [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01]] when saving an order for an overseas supplier if the line tax code does not align with the supplier's location [^r2][^r4][^r10]. Prior to patch 7.2.3-P6, Ledgerline's Fetch function invariably populated the domestic `VAT20-UK` default on purchase orders, requiring manual adjustment to reverse-charge codes for overseas vendors to avoid triggering the error [^r5][^r8][^r29].

## Meaning

The error displays the message `TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>)`, where the country code appended in brackets reflects the country recorded on the supplier account [^r1][^r14][^r18]. It indicates that an incorrect tax code was selected on a purchase order [^r17]. The message appears in the system status bar, in error dialogs, and within background process logs when orders are processed by batch jobs [^r16].

## Cause

`ERR-PO-0412` is triggered when a purchase order header fails validation against the vendor address record, verifying that the chosen tax code corresponds correctly to the location recorded on the master record for the supplier [^r15]. UK suppliers require a `-UK` tax code, while suppliers in any other country require an equivalent reverse-charge `-RC` code [^r4]. Prior to patch 7.2.3-P6, Fetch invariably set `VAT20-UK` on purchase orders, causing `ERR-PO-0412` on overseas supplier orders unless changed manually [^r29]. Frequent occurrences indicate that an overseas supplier was configured with domestic defaults [^r23].

## How to fix

To fix the error, verify the supplier country on the record and amend the line tax code to match the supplier's location [^r3][^r15]. For suppliers outside the UK, the user must change the line tax code to `VAT20-RC` for standard goods or `VAT5-RC` for reduced-rate items [^r9][^r20]. For a UK-registered supplier encountering the error, the tax code must be set to `VAT20-UK` [^r21]. After updating the line tax code, keep the cursor in the line details area and press F8 to save [^r3][^r22].

Users must never force a purchase order through using domestic tax codes for an overseas supplier account because doing so distorts tax returns [^r24]. Frequent occurrences of `ERR-PO-0412` require notifying the purchase ledger team to review and correct the supplier master profile [^r23].

## Raised by

The error is raised by the `po_save` service within [[services-pur-po]] during order validation when the entered tax code does not match the supplier country code or state [^r6][^r11][^r13]. It occurs when an overseas supplier retains an incompatible tax code such as `VAT20-UK` instead of `VAT20-RC` [^r2][^r12].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Default tax code population by Fetch (patch 7.2.3-P6 vs. earlier)**: Prior to patch 7.2.3-P6, Fetch invariably set `VAT20-UK` on purchase orders, causing `ERR-PO-0412` on orders for overseas vendors (such as suppliers based in the Netherlands or Poland) unless manually overwritten with a reverse-charge code [^r5][^r8][^r19][^r29]. Patch 7.2.3-P6 modified this behaviour [^r29].
* **Message text change (patch 7.2.3-P1 vs. superseded)**: Following patch 7.2.3-P1, the message text for `ERR-PO-0412` is `TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY`, with the supplier's country code appended in brackets [^r1][^r14][^r18]. Older training documentation and the superseded Ledgerline 7.0 manual used the message `TAX REGION DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER STATE` [^r14][^r25][^r27].
* **Resolution terminology (SOP-PUR-002 v1.4 vs. superseded)**: Under [[sop-pur-002|SOP-PUR-002]] v1.4, resolution requires amending the line tax code to `VAT20-RC` on PUR-PO-01 and pressing F8 [^r2][^r3]. In superseded SOP-PUR-002 v1.3 and the Ledgerline 7.0 manual, resolution was described as changing the tax region or regional authority assignment, or having accounts update the master record [^r26][^r27][^r28].

SUMMARY: UN 38.3 lithium battery transport certification rules, manual PO controls, renewal tracking, and ERP validation across Northbridge Cycles operations.
INFOBOX:
Topic: UN 38.3 Lithium Battery Certificates
Lead policy: POL-SUP-003, AMD-SUP-2026-02
Scope: Lithium-cell parts (BAT-*, hub motors, chargers)
ERP table: sup_cert (cert_type UN38.3)
Approval mandate: CERT OK comment on PO release
Current system status: Manual enforcement (PUR.CERT_CHK is N)
CONFLICTS:
- superseded | Under AMD-SUP-2026-02 and SOP-PUR-001, certificates must be issued within 12 months with valid_to at least 60 days past PO date | POL-SUP-003 §4 accepted certificates issued within 24 months, and SOP-PUR-001 v2.0 allowed reports within 3 months post-order | r5,r6,r13,r36,r51,r54,r57
- contradiction | Northbridge keeps PUR.CERT_CHK at 'N' following CR-2026-031 pending review in January 2027, relying on manual verification | Ledgerline 7.2.3-P6 introduced option 'B' to block orders with ERR-SUP-0208, and 7.2.3-P4 introduced advisory warning W-SUP-0207 | r14,r25,r26,r58,r59,r60
- future_dated | PUR.CERT_CHK remains 'N' under manual control today | Ledgerline 7.3 preview (planned March 2027) introduces hard blocking error ERR-SUP-0207 for missing, expired, or rejected certificates | r14,r50,r60
- superseded | UN 38.3 rules apply across all lithium-cell parts including packs, hub motors, and chargers | Superseded POL-PUR-001 v3.0 required UN 38.3 certificates only for battery packs | r8,r35,r56
BODY:
UN 38.3 certificates verify compliance with United Nations transport safety testing for lithium-cell components across Northbridge Cycles [^r8][^r35]. Since 1 September 2026, Northbridge requires all suppliers of lithium-cell items to hold a UN 38.3 report issued within the preceding 12 months and valid for at least 60 days beyond the purchase order date [^r5][^r13]. Because automated blocking remains disabled in Ledgerline ERP, purchasing staff and approvers must manually verify valid certificates before placing orders [^r11][^r14][^r47][^r60].

## Scope and Supplier Requirements

A verified UN 38.3 test report from an accredited testing laboratory, such as an ISO/IEC 17025 accredited facility, is mandatory for all vendors supplying lithium-cell parts [^r35]. This requirement applies to [[items-bat|battery packs]], [[items-mtr|hub motors]], [[items-chg|chargers]], and any item flagged with `cell_safety = 1` or marked lithium-cell in the item master [^r8][^r35]. Transport verification specifically requires the UN 38.3 test summary containing the accredited laboratory identification and manufacturer authorized signature rather than the full factory test report [^r15].

Certificates apply at the supplier level, but any change to part design, cell chemistry, casing seals, or battery management firmware invalidates existing testing and mandates a fresh UN 38.3 test report [^r10][^r16]. Under [[sop-prd-002|SOP-PRD-002]], an engineering change order introducing an alternative cell maker or altered pack design requires a verified UN 38.3 report logged in the technical archive prior to ECN release; failure to provide it halts pack sub-assembly at Leeds and quarantines incoming packs at Manchester [^r12]. Physical copies of UN 38.3 summaries must be maintained in dispatch office dangerous goods binders at both Manchester and Leeds, while superseded versions are moved to an archive directory [^r19].

## Purchasing and Quotation Controls

Prospective battery pack suppliers must submit a UN 38.3 transportation test summary report during onboarding evaluations [^r39]. Under [[sop-pur-006|SOP-PUR-006]], quotations for lithium-cell parts may only be compared among suppliers holding a valid UN 38.3 test certificate, and price alone must never determine selection [^r20]. A verified certificate must be attached to the supplier master record or entered against the quotation in Ledgerline before the quote can be marked acceptable [^r22]. If a quotation contains an expired, incomplete, or ambiguous certificate, the offer must be set aside immediately until verified by quality engineering [^r21]. Prospective supplier [[sup-brightcell-energy|Brightcell Energy]] currently lacks an active UN 38.3 test report while renewing with their laboratory, leaving their quotation pending until replacement documentation arrives [^r48].

Under onboarding checklist NBC-F-113, the proposer uploads the certificate with document reference and validity dates, which the senior buyer verifies before sign-off [^r23][^r24][^r30]. Following an incident on 28 July 2026 where an incoming abuse test failed on 400 battery packs with a 22-month-old test report from an unnotified cell maker change, Quality Manager [[user-pjansen|Pieter Jansen]] recommended tightening certificate validity [^r42][^r43][^r44]. Order approval now mandates entering `CERT OK` and the certificate reference (such as `CERT OK UN38.3-TR/VC/2026/118`) into the purchase order approval comment [^r45].

## ERP Records and System Enforcement

In Ledgerline ERP 7.2, certificate records are stored in the `sup_cert` table under `cert_type`, containing `doc_ref`, `valid_to`, `uploaded_by`, and `uploaded_on` [^r4]. Data is recorded in the supplier master under type `UN38.3` alongside the scanned attachment [^r29]. Active records in [[data-supplier-master|SUPPLIER_MASTER]] include [[user-lmoreno|Luis Moreno]]'s uploads for CC-SAL-0031 (certificate UN38.3-TR/CC/2026/044, valid to 2027-01-31) and AM-BIR-0008 (certificate UN38.3-TR/AM/2026/301, valid to 2027-06-30) [^r1][^r2]. [[sup-vc-ein-0042|Voltway Cells]] holds active certificate UN38.3-TR/VC/2026/118 valid through 31 March 2027, permitting direct receipt into WH-MAN-STR without quarantine and supporting technical construction files in Leeds [^r37][^r41].

Although Ledgerline 7.2.3-P6 introduced option `B` for parameter `PUR.CERT_CHK` to block purchase orders for lithium-cell items with [[err-sup-0208|ERR-SUP-0208]], this automated validation inspects only the `valid_to` date and ignores Northbridge issue date and safety margin rules [^r58][^r59]. Consequently, Northbridge maintains `PUR.CERT_CHK` at `N` under CR-2026-031 pending review in January 2027, meaning the ERP does not block purchase order entry on [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01]] for missing or invalid certificates [^r14][^r47][^r49][^r60]. Earlier release [[rn-7-2-3-p4|RN-7.2.3-P4]] provided an automated check raising advisory warning W-SUP-0207, but senior buyer sign-off on checklist NBC-F-113 and manual verification under [[sop-pur-001|SOP-PUR-001]] remain the sole operative controls [^r14][^r25][^r26][^r60].

## Expiry Monitoring and Supplier Status

Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]] §6.2, an expired UN 38.3 certificate counts as no certificate, requiring an immediate freeze on purchasing activities for regulated items [^r9][^r40]. Certificate expiry is tracked via batch job JOB-PUR-022 run on the first working day of each month with a 90-day horizon using the [[man-pur-72|MAN-PUR-72]] §22.6 report, which accepts a certificate type parameter [^r7][^r17][^r27]. Buyers issue template NBC-L-07 and enforce an order freeze at 60 days before expiry per [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]] [^r17].

If a certificate expires without renewal, buyers receive notification under subject `CERT EXPIRED - DO NOT ORDER`, and incoming consignments without active certification are quarantined on receipt [^r18]. As of October 2026, certificate expiry reporting highlights several suppliers:
* [[sup-nc-gda-0063|Nordic Cell Co. (NC-GDA-0063)]]: Certificate UN38.3-TR/NC/2025/090 expired on 2026-09-30, with lab renewal delayed until late November 2026; lithium orders remain manually halted [^r3][^r31][^r46][^r47].
* Tamar Energy Storage (TES-PLY-0144): Certificate UN38.3-TR/TE/2025/069 expires on 2026-11-30 [^r32].
* Saddleworth Charger Co. (SCC-BOL-0183): Certificate UN38.3-TR/SC/2025/067 expires on 2026-11-30 [^r33].
* Rheinfeld Cell Systems (RCS-STU-0151): Certificate UN38.3-TR/RC/2025/213 expires on 2026-12-15 [^r34].
* Voltway Cells: Quality is scheduled to request renewal documentation in January 2027 ahead of its March 2027 expiration [^r38].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Certificate issue age and validity margin (superseded):** Today, under AMD-SUP-2026-02 and SOP-PUR-001, certificates must be issued within the preceding 12 months with a `valid_to` date at least 60 days past the purchase order date [^r5][^r13]. Certificates between 12 and 24 months old became invalid for new purchase orders on 1 September 2026 [^r6]. Previously, [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] §4 and superseded POL-SUP-003 v2.2 accepted certificates issued within 24 months [^r36][^r51][^r54], and legacy procedure SOP-PUR-001 v2.0 allowed suppliers to provide reports within three months after their first order [^r57].
* **System enforcement vs manual controls (contradiction):** Today, Northbridge maintains parameter `PUR.CERT_CHK` at `N` following CR-2026-031 pending review in January 2027, relying on manual verification under SOP-PUR-001 and approval comments [^r11][^r14][^r45][^r60]. Ledgerline 7.2.3-P6 introduced option `B` to strictly block purchase orders for lithium-cell items with [[err-sup-0208|ERR-SUP-0208]], and release 7.2.3-P4 added advisory warning W-SUP-0207; however, because the ERP validates only `valid_to` dates and does not enforce Northbridge's issue date or 60-day margin rules, automated blocking remains turned off [^r25][^r26][^r49][^r58][^r59][^r60].
* **ERP 7.3 blocking error (future_dated):** Today, Ledgerline parameter `PUR.CERT_CHK` remains `N` [^r14][^r60]. In planned Ledgerline ERP 7.3 (effective 2027-03-01), missing, expired, or rejected UN 38.3 records are scheduled to raise hard blocking error [[err-sup-0207|ERR-SUP-0207]] [^r50].
* **Regulated component scope (superseded):** Today, UN 38.3 rules apply across all lithium-cell parts including packs, hub motors, and chargers [^r8][^r35]. Under superseded policy POL-PUR-001 v3.0, only battery packs required UN 38.3 certificates, excluding hub motors and chargers [^r56].

- superseded | po_fetch populates VAT20-UK for GB suppliers and VAT20-RC for non-GB suppliers | po_fetch always returned VAT20-UK regardless of supplier country | r44,r87
- superseded | Services operate via HTTP POST under /ll72/svc/ using session tokens and YAML service definitions | Purchase order creation used legacy RPC PO_ENTRY_SAVE with LL6-RPC transport and fixed CHAR fields | r22,r23,r72
BODY:
The `po_*` service group handles the purchase order lifecycle in Ledgerline ERP, covering order creation, line default retrieval, approval workflow, release, amendment, query, and cancellation [^r15][^r72][^r85]. Operating within module `PUR`, write operations execute validation, tax computation, stock on-order tracking, and budget reservation procedures [^r13][^r19][^r27][^r73]. For integrations and interactive screens alike, order creation via `po_save` enforces validation tokens obtained through `po_fetch` to ensure supplier and item parameters remain synchronized [^r1][^r80][^r81].

## Services

### po_fetch
The `po_fetch` service retrieves default parameters for a proposed purchase order line on screen [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01]] [^r12][^r39]. It invokes stored procedure `sp_fetch_tok_new` and returns a single-use `fetch_tok` token valid exclusively for the specified supplier and item combination [^r1][^r43]. The service sets `tax_cd` to `VAT20-UK` when the supplier country is GB, and to `VAT20-RC` for any other supplier country [^r87].
* **Kind**: Read [^r39].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_fetch` [^r39].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r40].
* **Required fields**: `sup_cd`, `itm_cd` [^r41].
* **Optional fields**: `pr_no` [^r41].
* **Return envelope**: `rc` (`S`, `W`, or `E`), `err_cd`, `msg`, and `data` [^r3][^r42].
* **Errors**: [[err-sup-0030|ERR-SUP-0030]], `ERR-SEC-0001`, `ERR-SYS-0421`, `ERR-SYS-0422`, `ERR-SYS-0503` [^r45][^r46].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_fetch.yaml` [^r39].

### po_save
The `po_save` service creates or updates purchase orders from screen [[screen-pur-po-01|PUR-PO-01]] [^r72]. It executes database procedures `sp_fetch_tok_chk`, `sp_po_hdr_save`, `sp_appr_route`, `sp_budget_chk`, `sp_budget_commit`, `sp_doc_no_next`, `sp_ntf_enqueue`, `sp_po_status_set`, `sp_tax_compute`, and `sp_tax_region_chk` [^r73]. The service validates need-by dates, line quantities, tax codes matching the supplier country, purchase requisition linkage, item and quantity conformance against the PR, and the 50,000 gross limit on direct (`DIR`) orders without a PR [^r4][^r5][^r14]. External callers must include `fetch_tok` from `po_fetch`, or the service rejects the request with [[err-scr-0221|ERR-SCR-0221]] [^r9][^r80][^r81]. If saved against a closed cost centre, the document is retained in draft status `DR` with warning [[w-cc-114|W-CC-114]] instead of failing [^r2][^r82][^r84]. Responses return message `<PO NO> SAVED` with `data.status` reflecting `DR`, `PA`, or `AP` [^r74].
* **Kind**: Write [^r13][^r72].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_save` [^r72].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r72].
* **Required fields**: `sup_cd`, `itm_cd`, `qty`, `rate`, `tax_cd`, `cc_cd`, `need_dt` [^r13][^r86].
* **Optional fields**: `po_type`, `pr_no`, `whs_cd`, `fetch_tok`, `client_ref` [^r2][^r86].
* **Errors and warnings**: [[err-scr-0221|ERR-SCR-0221]], [[err-po-0412|ERR-PO-0412]], [[err-po-0610|ERR-PO-0610]], [[err-sup-0030|ERR-SUP-0030]], [[err-sup-0031|ERR-SUP-0031]], `ERR-TAX-0101`, [[w-cc-114|W-CC-114]] [^r5][^r9][^r10][^r11][^r14][^r81][^r84].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_save.yaml` [^r72].

### po_get
The `po_get` service retrieves full header and line details for an existing purchase order [^r15][^r47].
* **Kind**: Read [^r47].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_get` [^r47].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r47].
* **Required fields**: `po_no` [^r48].
* **Optional fields**: None [^r48].
* **Return envelope**: `rc` (`S`, `W`, or `E`), `err_cd`, `msg`, and `data` [^r3][^r49].
* **Errors**: `ERR-PO-0001`, `ERR-SEC-0001`, `ERR-SYS-0421`, `ERR-SYS-0422`, `ERR-SYS-0503` [^r50].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_get.yaml` [^r47].

### po_search
The `po_search` service queries purchase orders by search criteria and returns matching order headers, including the `created_by` audit attribute [^r15][^r75][^r83].
* **Kind**: Read [^r75].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_search` [^r76].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r76].
* **Required fields**: None [^r77].
* **Optional fields**: `sup_cd`, `itm_cd`, `status`, `client_ref`, `from_dt` [^r77].
* **Return envelope**: `rc` (`S`, `W`, or `E`), `err_cd`, `msg`, and `data` [^r3][^r78].
* **Errors**: `ERR-SEC-0001`, `ERR-SYS-0421`, `ERR-SYS-0422`, `ERR-SYS-0503` [^r79].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_search.yaml` [^r75].

### po_hist
The `po_hist` service reads historical purchase orders for a specified inventory item on screen [[screen-pur-poh-02|PUR-POH-02]] [^r15][^r51].
* **Kind**: Read [^r51].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_hist` [^r51].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r52].
* **Required fields**: `itm_cd` [^r53].
* **Optional fields**: `sup_cd` [^r53].
* **Return envelope**: `rc` (`S`, `W`, or `E`), `err_cd`, `msg`, and `data` [^r3][^r54].
* **Errors**: `ERR-SEC-0001`, `ERR-SYS-0421`, `ERR-SYS-0422`, `ERR-SYS-0503` [^r55].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_hist.yaml` [^r51].

### po_pending_appr
The `po_pending_appr` service lists purchase orders awaiting authorization within the approval inbox [^r16][^r56][^r57].
* **Kind**: Read [^r57].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_pending_appr` [^r57].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r58].
* **Required fields**: None [^r59].
* **Optional fields**: `approver` [^r16][^r59].
* **Return envelope**: `rc` (`S`, `W`, or `E`), `err_cd`, `msg`, and `data` [^r3][^r60].
* **Errors**: `ERR-SEC-0001`, `ERR-SYS-0421`, `ERR-SYS-0422`, `ERR-SYS-0503` [^r61].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_pending_appr.yaml` [^r56].

### po_approve
The `po_approve` service approves purchase orders in pending approval status `PA` from screen [[screen-pur-poa-04|PUR-POA-04]] [^r6][^r29].
* **Kind**: Write [^r29].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_approve` [^r29].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r30].
* **Required fields**: `po_no` [^r17][^r31].
* **Optional fields**: `comment` [^r17][^r31].
* **Return envelope**: `rc` (`S`, `W`, or `E`), `err_cd`, `msg`, and `data` [^r3][^r32].
* **Errors**: `ERR-PO-0001`, `ERR-PO-0702`, [[err-apr-0003|ERR-APR-0003]], [[err-apr-0004|ERR-APR-0004]], `ERR-SEC-0001`, `ERR-SYS-0421`, `ERR-SYS-0422`, `ERR-SYS-0503` [^r6][^r17][^r33][^r34].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_approve.yaml` [^r29].

### po_reject
The `po_reject` service rejects purchase orders awaiting approval on screen [[screen-pur-poa-04|PUR-POA-04]] [^r62]. Rejection requires an explicit reason and fails if the document is not in `PA` status [^r6][^r18][^r64].
* **Kind**: Write [^r62].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_reject` [^r62].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r63].
* **Required fields**: `po_no`, `comment` [^r18][^r64].
* **Optional fields**: None [^r64].
* **Return envelope**: `rc` (`S`, `W`, or `E`), `err_cd`, `msg`, and `data` [^r3][^r65].
* **Errors**: `ERR-PO-0702`, `ERR-SEC-0001`, `ERR-SYS-0421`, `ERR-SYS-0422`, `ERR-SYS-0503` [^r66].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_reject.yaml` [^r62].

### po_release
The `po_release` service releases approved orders in status `AP` via procedures `sp_po_status_set`, `sp_stk_onorder_upd`, and `sp_ntf_enqueue`, updating stock on-order quantities and triggering notification e-mails to the vendor [^r7][^r19][^r67][^r70][^r71].
* **Kind**: Write [^r19][^r67].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_release` [^r67].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r68].
* **Required fields**: `po_no` [^r19][^r69].
* **Optional fields**: None [^r69].
* **Errors**: `ERR-PO-0001`, `ERR-PO-0715` [^r7][^r19].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_release.yaml` [^r67].

### po_amend
The `po_amend` service modifies existing purchase orders from screen [[screen-pur-pom-06|PUR-POM-06]] using stored procedures `sp_tax_compute`, `sp_budget_chk`, `sp_budget_commit`, `sp_appr_route`, and `sp_ntf_enqueue` [^r24][^r27]. It rejects attempts to amend orders in closed, cancelled, or rejected statuses (`CN`, `RJ`, `CL`) [^r8][^r20]. Amendments that increase order commitments beyond approved limits return the document to `PA` status, while modifications pointing to a closed cost centre return it to `DR` with advisory warning [[w-cc-114|W-CC-114]] [^r20][^r28].
* **Kind**: Write [^r20][^r24].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_amend` [^r24].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r25].
* **Required fields**: `po_no` [^r20][^r26].
* **Optional fields**: `qty`, `need_dt`, `cc_cd` [^r20][^r26].
* **Errors and warnings**: `ERR-PO-0001`, [[err-po-0801|ERR-PO-0801]], `ERR-TAX-0101`, [[err-cc-0009|ERR-CC-0009]], `ERR-BUD-0207`, [[err-apr-0009|ERR-APR-0009]], [[w-cc-114|W-CC-114]] [^r8][^r20][^r84].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_amend.yaml` [^r24].

### po_cancel
The `po_cancel` service cancels an order from screen [[screen-pur-pom-06|PUR-POM-06]], invoking `sp_stk_onorder_upd` and `sp_po_status_set` to release stock on-order allocations [^r21][^r35][^r37]. The system does not transmit cancellation notifications to the supplier [^r37]. Orders already in `CN`, `RJ`, or `CL` status cannot be cancelled [^r8][^r38].
* **Kind**: Write [^r21][^r35].
* **Endpoint**: `POST /ll72/svc/po_cancel` [^r35].
* **Authentication**: Session token in `X-LL-Session` header and an authorized role [^r35].
* **Required fields**: `po_no`, `reason` [^r21][^r36].
* **Optional fields**: None [^r36].
* **Return envelope**: `rc` (`S`, `W`, or `E`), `err_cd`, `msg`, and `data` [^r3][^r36].
* **Errors**: `ERR-PO-0001`, [[err-po-0801|ERR-PO-0801]] [^r8][^r21][^r38].
* **Source file**: `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_cancel.yaml` [^r35].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Today's rule**: Service `po_fetch` sets `tax_cd` to `VAT20-UK` when the supplier country is GB, and to `VAT20-RC` for any other supplier country as of Ledgerline 7.2.3-P6 [^r87].
* **Older rule**: Service `po_fetch` always returned `tax_cd` as `VAT20-UK` regardless of supplier country, requiring manual adjustment to `VAT20-RC` on `po_save` to avoid [[err-po-0412|ERR-PO-0412]] [^r44].
* **Sources and dates**: `RN-7.2.3-P6` (2026-10-26) vs `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_fetch.yaml` (2025-01-15) [^r44][^r87].
* **Kind**: `superseded` [^r87].

* **Today's rule**: Ledgerline 7.2 services operate via HTTP POST endpoints under `/ll72/svc/` using `X-LL-Session` authentication tokens and structured service definitions [^r24][^r30][^r72].
* **Older rule**: Under legacy Ledgerline 6.4, purchase order creation utilized RPC service `PO_ENTRY_SAVE` with `LL6-RPC` transport and fixed CHAR fields `VENDOR_NO`, `ITEM_NO`, `QTY`, `PRICE`, `TAX_REGION`, `CC`, and `DUE_DATE`, returning `RETCODE` and `DOCNO` [^r22][^r23].
* **Sources and dates**: `04_service_definitions/_legacy_6x/PO_ENTRY_SAVE.xml` (superseded 2015) vs `04_service_definitions/purchase/po_save.yaml` (Ledgerline 7.0/7.2) [^r22][^r72].
* **Kind**: `superseded` [^r22].

BODY:
PUR-PO-01 is the Ledgerline purchasing screen used to create, edit, and park single-line purchase orders [^r9][^r11][^r22]. It supports standard orders referencing an approved purchase request and direct orders without a request, but does not allow direct supplier dispatch or immediate authorisation from the entry form [^r1][^r6][^r22]. Users must run the Fetch function (`F3`) after populating or changing the supplier and item fields, or the subsequent save will be rejected [^r2][^r7][^r28][^r35].

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Screen code | PUR-PO-01 |
| Title | Purchase Order Entry |
| Menu path | Menu Purchase > Order entry [^r11] |
| Permitted roles | PUR-EXEC, PUR-SR, SYS-ADMIN [^r11] |
| Primary services | `po_fetch`, `po_save` [^r12][^r18][^r20] |
| Order types | `STD` (Standard), `DIR` (Direct) [^r1][^r6] |

## Fields

Each purchase order raised on PUR-PO-01 accommodates exactly one line item in the grid [^r9].

* **PO NO (`po_no`)**: Purchase order document identifier; read-only [^r13].
* **PO TYPE (`po_type`)**: Mandatory order classification [^r13]. Supported values are `STD` for orders referencing an approved purchase request and `DIR` for direct low-value orders raised without a request [^r1][^r6]. `DIR` orders referencing a purchase request trigger error ERR-PO-0611, while `DIR` orders exceeding £50,000 gross value trigger [[err-po-0610|ERR-PO-0610]] [^r10][^r16].
* **SOURCE PR (`pr_no`)**: Optional request reference; populated with the approved request number when raising `STD` orders [^r1][^r18][^r33].
* **SUP CD (`sup_cd`)**: Mandatory supplier code [^r13][^r18].
* **ITEM CD (`itm_cd`)**: Mandatory item number [^r13][^r18]. The component lookup may experience query latency across large item families unless restricted by initial character input [^r27].
* **QTY (`qty`)**: Mandatory order quantity; populated by `po_fetch` when linked to a request [^r12][^r13].
* **RATE (`rate`)**: Mandatory unit price; populated by `po_fetch` from contracted rates [^r12][^r13]. Pressing `F2` in this field opens a historical rate look-up window displaying previous agreed purchase rates, references, and statuses for the selected supplier and item, transferring the selected value directly into the line [^r25][^r26].
* **PAY TERM (`pt_cd`)**: Payment terms; retrieved via `po_fetch`; read-only [^r12][^r13].
* **TAX CD (`tax_cd`)**: Mandatory tax classification [^r13]. Populated by `po_fetch` with default `VAT20-UK` for GB suppliers and `VAT20-RC` for suppliers in all other countries [^r46].
* **CC CD (`cc_cd`)**: Mandatory cost centre code; populated by `po_fetch` [^r12][^r13].
* **NEED DT (`need_dt`)**: Mandatory required delivery date; populated by `po_fetch` [^r12][^r13].
* **STATUS (`status`)**: Header purchase order status; read-only [^r13]. Possible values include Draft (`DR`), Pending Approval (`PA`), or Approved (`AP`) [^r4][^r17].
* **DELIVERY REMARKS**: Text field for special transit or carriage instructions to alert receiving personnel to pallet drops or oversized deliveries [^r40].

## Keys and services

* **F2 (Rate History)**: Accessible within the Rate field; invokes the previous rate enquiry pop-up for the active supplier and item [^r25]. Cancelling returns to the field without updating values [^r26].
* **F3 (Fetch / `po_fetch`)**: Executes read service `po_fetch` under [[services-pur-po|PUR po services]] using mandatory inputs `sup_cd` and `itm_cd`, and optional input `pr_no` [^r12][^r18]. It retrieves the contract rate, lead periods, descriptions, payment terms, cost centre, need date, quantity, and tax code defaults (`VAT20-UK` for GB suppliers, `VAT20-RC` for all other countries) [^r12][^r18][^r34][^r46].
* **F8 (Save / `po_save`)**: Invokes backend service `po_save` to record order details [^r20]. Upon write completion, the bottom status bar displays `SAVED` regardless of whether the document remains uncommitted or stuck in status `DR`, `PA`, or `AP` [^r4][^r37].
* **Order submission**: Submitting an order transfers it to [[screen-pur-poa-04|PUR-POA-04]] for approval [^r23]. Any subsequent line modification returns the order to an unapproved state [^r23]. If rejected during approval, the order returns to PUR-PO-01 with notification for the creator [^r24].

## Messages

* **[[err-scr-0221|ERR-SCR-0221]] (`FETCH NOT DONE`)**: Raised on save when the user has not performed an explicit `F3` Fetch action for the current supplier and item combination, or if either field was modified after fetching [^r2][^r7][^r14][^r28][^r35].
* **[[err-po-0412|ERR-PO-0412]] (`TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY`)**: Raised on save when an order for an overseas supplier retains a UK tax code instead of a reverse-charge code [^r3][^r8][^r15][^r19].
* **[[err-po-0610|ERR-PO-0610]]**: Raised on save if a direct purchase order (`DIR`) exceeds the gross monetary limit of £50,000 [^r10][^r16].
* **ERR-PO-0611**: Raised on save if a direct purchase order (`DIR`) references a purchase request [^r10].
* **[[err-sup-0208|ERR-SUP-0208]] (`UN38.3 CERTIFICATE MISSING OR EXPIRED`)**: Raised on save when system parameter `PUR.CERT_CHK` is set to `B` and an order is saved for an item flagged as a lithium cell whose supplier lacks a valid UN 38.3 certificate on the order date, refusing the save [^r47].
* **[[w-cc-114|W-CC-114]]**: Amber warning banner displayed when saving an order allocated to a closed cost centre [^r17][^r21][^r29]. The order is stored in Draft status (`DR`) with editable lines, commitment is blocked, and the status bar displays `SAVED` [^r5][^r17][^r21][^r29].
* **W-SUP-0207 (`UN38.3 CERTIFICATE MISSING OR EXPIRED`)**: Advisory status bar warning generated when system parameter `PUR.CERT_CHK` is set to `Y` and an order is saved for an item flagged as a lithium cell whose supplier lacks a valid UN 38.3 certificate on the order date [^r30][^r31]. The warning is non-fatal and allows the order to save [^r31][^r32].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Tax code defaulting on Fetch**: From 26 October 2026 under patch 7.2.3-P6, `po_fetch` automatically sets `tax_cd` to `VAT20-UK` for GB suppliers and `VAT20-RC` for suppliers in all other countries (`RN-7.2.3-P6`) [^r46]. Previously, Fetch always defaulted to `VAT20-UK` regardless of supplier origin, requiring manual entry of `VAT20-RC` for overseas vendors to avoid [[err-po-0412|ERR-PO-0412]] (`SOP-PUR-002 v1.4`, `MAN-PUR-72 v7.2.3`, `MAN-SCR-72 v7.2.3`, `po_fetch.yaml`, `QRC-02 v2026.1`) (`superseded`) [^r3][^r8][^r15][^r19][^r36][^r44].
* **UN 38.3 certificate check blocking**: From 26 October 2026 under patch 7.2.3-P6, if system parameter `PUR.CERT_CHK` is set to `B`, saving an order for a lithium-cell item without a valid certificate is refused with [[err-sup-0208|ERR-SUP-0208]] (`RN-7.2.3-P6`) [^r47]. Under patch 7.2.3-P4 (14 September 2026), validation was governed by setting `PUR.CERT_CHK` to `Y`, which only produced an advisory warning `W-SUP-0207` in the status bar while permitting the save (`RN-7.2.3-P4`) (`superseded`) [^r30][^r31][^r32]. From March 2027 under Ledgerline ERP 7.3 preview, a non-compliant or expired certificate on any cell line will hard-block the entire document with [[err-sup-0207|ERR-SUP-0207]] (`RN-7.3-PREVIEW`) (`future_dated`) [^r42].
* **Fetch requirement before save**: Today, `F3` Fetch must be executed for the identical supplier and item combination prior to saving, otherwise save is halted with [[err-scr-0221|ERR-SCR-0221]] (`MAN-PUR-72 v7.2.3`, `RN-7.2.3`, `QRC-02 v2026.1`) [^r7][^r28][^r35]. In obsolete 2016 intranet guidance (`11_training/intranet_export_2016/how_to_raise_an_order.html`), Fetch was described as optional with rates entered manually (`superseded`) [^r39].
* **Single-line versus multi-line orders**: Today, PUR-PO-01 permits only one item line per purchase order document (`MAN-PUR-72 v7.2.3`) [^r9]. From March 2027 under Ledgerline ERP 7.3 preview, PUR-PO-01 will support multi-line purchase orders on a single document header (`RN-7.3-PREVIEW`) (`future_dated`) [^r41].
